messages:
maria: Starting onboarding for Astraon-6B (hf-converted int4). Quick sanity run shows deterministic diffs vs float32 on a small prompt set — early EOS and some token aliasing.
ash: Can you paste the conversion command and one failing sample?
maria: convert cmd: `python tools/convert.py --src=orig-gf --dst=hf --model=astraon-6b --quant=int4 --token-map=auto --keep-proj-order`
maria: Failing sample (short):
```
Prompt: "List prime numbers under 20"
HF top tokens sequence: [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, <eos>]
Astraon-int4 seq:       [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, <eos>]  <-- EOS at index 5 (early stop)
```
devon: Seen similar when headwise rotary scale or proj-order differs after conversion. Could be head-proj ordering or per-head rotary frequency scale mismatch.
sasha: Also check tokenizer normalization and any invisible chars. A shifted token id or extra sentinel can trigger early eos.
maria: Tokenizer config we used: {'normalizer': 'nfkc', 'add_prefix_space': False, 'bos_token': '<s>'}. Conversion didn't explicitly supply a token-map override.
nash: Quick diff: run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').encode('List prime numbers under 20').ids)"` on both artifacts (orig vs converted).
nash: Also dump the raw ids for the HF baseline and the converted model to confirm mapping.
ops: Repro'd locally with hf-converter v0.9. If I swap proj-order during conversion (flag --proj-order=swap), top1 accuracy improves but EOS early-stop persists for some prompts.
devon: If proj-order fixes logits but not EOS, I suspect rotary phase/headwise scaling. Try toggling per-head rotary scale or applying a small phase offset correction.
maria: Ran a quick patch: forcibly set per-head rotary_scale = 1.0 for all heads. Result: EOS shift moves later (better) but punctuation probabilities get noisy.
sasha: Could be kvcache key misalignment too — if kv keys index-shift you can produce weird attention that pushes EOS. Dump KV keys for first 4 steps with generate(dump_kv=True).
maria: KV dump shows consistent head offsets of +1 token for even heads.
triage-bot: INF-4521 created and assigned to @maria with label triage-needed :mag: — added logs and repro command.
nash: For immediate mitigation, try: 1) enforce tokenizer mapping overrides (--token-map explicit) 2) preserve proj-order from orig model 3) align rotary per-head scaling to baseline. Test each change in isolation.
devon: I'm kicking off a small eval job: 200 seed prompts, measure EOS position delta, token-level edit distance, and top-1 accuracy. Will upload CSV to the ticket.
ops: FYI, a run with --proj-order=preserve + manual tokenizer map reduced early-EOS count by ~47% in my quick loop. Reproduced on 3 seeds.
maria: Adding the repro snippet to the ticket and will try devon's eval harness.
sasha: Useful short scripts: 
```
# token id dump
python - <<EOF
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_orig.json').encode('a b').ids)
print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer_conv.json').encode('a b').ids)
EOF
```
nash: Also share a tiny logits diff snippet if possible (top5 per step) so we can see whether EOS is boosted or other tokens suppressed.
maria: Will attach top5 diffs. For now putting current hypothesis in INF-4521: combined proj-order + headwise-rotary-scale drift + tokenizer normalization mismatch.
devon: If hypothesis holds, next steps: add conversion unit test comparing token ids + per-head rotary statistics (mean/var of rotary angles) vs baseline.
ops: I'll pin a temporary fallback to a float32 variant for heavy traffic routes until we ship conversion fix.
nash: :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — will update ticket when eval finishes. :rocket:
